conflicts: Speed: Singer's product page says 1100/min; the shared HD 6700C and HD 6705C manual says 1000 +/- 50 rpm. We use the manual figure; Amazon and dealers repeat 1,100.

Warranty: Singer's product page and linked PDF say 25/1 (25-year frame, 1-year parts); our earlier 25/2/90 is a tier Singer assigns to the 4452, 4432 and 3342, and Singer's coverage page does not name the 6700C. Amazon shows '1 Year Manufacturer'. The PDF names no model.

Needle up/down: the shared manual documents a Needle Up/Down button, the 6700C product page does not list it, and the 6800C and 6620C pages do. Our earlier 'none' came from a blog. Unresolved, so left [verify].

Stitch count: Singer's comparison page gives 200 built-in stitches and 411 applications; the product page gives 411 applications, and its prose also says 586, a figure that matches the 6800C page. Left [verify]; 586 is not used.
Lettering: Singer's product page lists 1 lettering font and its comparison page lists 2; the manual shows a Block Font at 7 mm letter height.
Throat: 6.4 in is Singer's 'needle to tower' figure, not stated as needle to body, so throat is [verify] on the rule 11 scale.
Weight: 7 kg (15.4 lb) in the shared manual against 14.6 lb on Amazon and 16.3 lb on one blog.
Start/stop: the shared manual documents a Start/Stop button; the product page does not list one. Unverified for the 6700C alone.
Sibling pages: Singer's comparison page gives the 6800C 8.3 in of throat and 1,050 spm while its 6800C product page says 6.4 in and 1100/min; read sibling rows with that in mind.
Page status on 2026-10-02 (page wording only): the Singer 6600C page returned 404 and the 6800C and 6620C pages read Out of Stock; the 6700C page showed the machine for sale.

ownerThemes.theme: Several owner help threads describe top thread looping mid-seam on a new 6700C after a clean test swatch; the answers point to rethreading through the tension discs, cleaning lint from the bobbin area, and the small bobbin case screw.
Walmart owner reviews (4 of 5 stars over about 200 reviews) call it smooth and good for quilting, curtains and clothing, with one experienced sewer saying it is not a first machine.
PatternReview members discussing the launch of Singer's computerized Heavy Duty line note that earlier HD models were all mechanical and question what the electronics add on a budget frame.

editorial.verdict: A metal-frame computerized machine with 10 feet and a walking foot, but Singer's own pages disagree on speed, stitch count and needle up/down.
editorial.whoFor: A beginner or returning sewer who wants a walking foot, a speed lever and lettering on a metal-frame machine.
editorial.skipIf: You want a confirmed thread cutter or needle up/down button, a plain stitch count before you buy, or dials rather than an LCD on a heavy fabric machine.

faqs.q: Is the Singer HD6700C a good sewing machine, according to owners?
faqs.a: The evidence is thin: 17 voices, 16 first-hand, from 16 Reddit threads and 1 retailer page. Threading (6 voices, 3 positive and 3 negative) and tension (5 voices, all negative) are the recurring themes, with owners describing a top thread that slips out of place and a top tension dial that seems to do nothing. One Amazon owner hemmed work pants and stitched a canvas tote without trouble, and 3 voices praise low noise. Amazon shows 4.4 of 5 from 980 ratings (seen 2026-10-02), pooled across listings of this machine, and Reddit leans toward help requests, so problems are over-represented.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Singer 6700C and the 6800C?
faqs.a: On Singer's pages the 6800C adds a thread cutter button, Needle Up/Down and more stitch applications (586 on its page against 411 for the 6700C). Singer's pages also disagree on the 6800C throat (6.4 in on its product page, 8.3 in on the comparison page) and speed (1100/min against 1,050), and the 6800C page showed out of stock on 2026-10-02. These are maker-page figures that do not agree with each other [verify].

faqs.q: Does the Singer 6700C have an automatic thread cutter?
faqs.a: Singer's product page lists a tie-off button and no thread cutter. The 6800C page lists a Thread Cutter Button that trims top and bottom threads. The manual's thread knife is a hand cutter.

faqs.q: Does the Singer 6700C have needle up/down?
faqs.a: Unresolved. The shared HD 6700C and HD 6705C manual documents a Needle Up/Down button, the 6700C product page does not list one, and the 6800C and 6620C pages do. Confirm with the seller [verify].

faqs.q: Does the Singer 6700C come with a walking foot?
faqs.a: Yes. The even feed (walking) foot is one of 10 feet on Singer's accessory list, along with open toe and cording feet. One Reddit thread mentions the walking foot without a verdict, so we hold no owner view on it.

faqs.q: How many stitches does the Singer 6700C have?
faqs.a: Singer's comparison page says 200 built-in stitches and 411 stitch applications. The product page says 411 applications and its prose also says 586, which looks like the 6800C number. We list the disagreement and do not state a plain count [verify].

faqs.q: Is the Singer 6700C good for quilting?
faqs.a: Singer claims a generous C space for larger projects like quilts, and gives the throat as 6.4 in, worded needle to tower rather than needle to body [verify]. One Amazon owner wishes the throat were bigger and uses a quilting machine for larger projects. Treat larger quilts with caution.

faqs.q: What are the specs of the Singer 6700C?
faqs.a: Singer's product page says 1100 stitches per minute and the shared HD 6700C and HD 6705C manual says 1000 +/- 50, so speed is [verify]. The manual gives 7 kg (15.4 lb) against 14.6 lb on Amazon, a 6 mm presser foot lift and a 0.7 A, 120 V electrical rating with no wattage published. Heavy Duty is a series name, not a duty rating, and the 6.4 in throat is needle to tower [verify].

faqs.q: What is the price of the Singer 6700C?
faqs.a: Singer's page showed a $419.99 list price with a $329.99 sale price, and Sewing Machines Plus showed $329.99 on 2026-09-29 against a $419.99 regular price. Singer's extension table bundle was $349.99 against $488.98 original. Prices drift weekly, so use the price band on this page as the stable guide.
